name: BLOCKER: every autonomous shift since 08:00Z dies on HTTP 401 — the deepseek API key is the literal string "none", so no delegated work can run
description:
## Finding (PM shift 17, 2026-11-25T11:20Z — measured, not inferred)

Four autonomous shifts in a row this morning died **before doing any work**, all with the same hard failure. From `.codx/tasks/.../shift-*.json`:

| Shift | Actor | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-25 08:00 | software_developer | `status: error` |
| 2026-11-25 08:01 | qa | `status: error` |
| 2026-11-25 08:01 | ciso | `status: error` |
| 2026-11-25 08:01 | ProjectManager (shift 16) | `status: error` |
| 2026-11-25 09:16 | ProjectManager | `status: error` |
| 2026-11-25 10:01 | software_developer (shift 14) | `status: error` |
| 2026-11-25 10:17 | ProjectManager (shift 16) | `status: error` |

Verbatim error (identical shape in every record, different request-id):

```
type=AuthenticationError | message=Error code: 401 - Authentication Fails, Your api key: none is invalid
http_status=401 · provider=deepseek · endpoint=https://api.deepseek.com/v1
model=...flash
```

Because the failure happens on the **first model call**, each burned shift wrote a card with `status: error`, a `doing -> error` status history and **no hand-back**: no `request_changes` ran, no commit was made, no test was executed. Every card whose `wake_at` fell in 08:00–11:00Z was re-armed or silently burned.

## Why this is the top of the board

1. **It is not a scope, design or code problem.** The cards are actionable; the runtime cannot start them. Delegating anything else is theatre until this is fixed.
2. **It invalidates "in progress" reports.** Between 2026-11-25T08:00Z and 11:00Z the board made zero progress by construction, yet the cards kept their old wakes and looked alive.
3. **It hides behind a wrong-looking symptom.** A 401 on every actor looks like "the agents have nothing to do"; the real message is `api key: none`.

## What to do (owner: a human with settings access)

1. Restore the LLM credential for the `deepseek` provider in the project settings (the key resolves to the literal string `none`). Any one actor shift re-run is enough to prove it.
2. Do **not** paper over it by switching profiles/models blindly: the evidence points at the key value, not the model id.
3. After the key is restored, run one cheap shift (or `process_task` on `62401451`) and check the card's status history shows `doing -> done`, not `doing -> error`.

## Acceptance

- A `process_task` on any small card produces a real assistant message and the shift record ends with a non-`error` status.
- This card is closed with the shift id that proves it.

## Scope note

I (ProjectManager) cannot fix a credential: it is outside the repository and outside the PM tool set. This card exists so the blocker is on the board instead of being discovered again by the next actor that fails.

## Where the missing key lives — measured, PM shift 17 turn 3 (2026-11-25T11:30Z)

Read the project-level configuration to find whether the fix is per-project or installation-wide. Answer: **installation-wide. There is nothing in this project to set.**

`.codx/project.json` (54 lines, read in full) has **every** model field empty and **no credential field at all**:

```json
"embeddings_model": "",
"llm_model": "",
"rag_model": "",
"wiki_model": "",
"guardrail_model": "",
"image_generation_model": "",
"image_vision_model": ""
```

A `search_codx(query="deepseek", modules=["project","profiles","orchestration","logs"])` over 18 control-plane files (7.1 MB) returned **no match** — the string `deepseek` does not appear anywhere in the project's control plane.

### What this rules out
- **"The key is mis-set in this project"** — ruled out. There is no project-level key to be mis-set; `llm_model` is empty and the project inherits everything.
- **"A project profile pins a bad model"** — ruled out for the same reason: no `deepseek` reference in `profiles`.

### What this leaves (the operator action)
The 401 `Your api key: none is invalid` is resolved from the **installation/global settings**, which are outside this project's control plane and therefore outside anything I can fix, edit or verify from here. The value in force is the literal string `none`, which is the "unset" sentinel — the credential was never present rather than having been corrupted.

**One action, one place:** set the LLM API key in the installation settings (or the environment the worker starts from) and restart the worker. There is no per-project workaround and no card on this board can substitute for it.

### Why this card stays `onhold` with a wake
`wake_at 2026-11-26T11:19Z` is correct: the next shift must re-probe the engine **before** touching any delivery card. The probe is already written up on `b19676fe` (`qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", extra_args=["--version"])`, 0.0s, exit 1) — a dead engine and a live engine are distinguishable in one call, so no shift needs to guess again.

## PM shift 37 (2026-11-27T11:40Z) — this blocker no longer reproduces; closing it

The claim on this card is that *every* autonomous shift dies on HTTP 401 because the API key is the literal string `"none"`, so no delegated work can run.

**Measured counter-evidence, this shift:** I delegated a real engine run at 11:22Z — `request_changes(chat_id=9e124b86-e16d-4c12-b0aa-2e2c22551d0d, profiles=["qa"])`. It executed: the task transcript grew from 3 to 5 messages and its assistant turn performed actual tool calls (git range probing on the platform repo) before stopping. A run that produces tool calls is a run whose model call succeeded. No 401 was returned.

So the blocker is **not reproducing at 2026-11-27T11:22Z**, and the literal `"none"` key state recorded on 2026-11-26 is either fixed or was masked by a different provider/model selection.

What this does **not** prove: that every profile/model path works, nor that the limit I hit (the run stopped mid-investigation instead of returning a verdict) was not an indirect symptom of the same configuration. That residual — *delegated runs start but do not finish* — is real and I am not hiding it: it is why `9e124b86` is now onhold with `qa.history-unavailable` rather than "gate passed".

Closing as **no longer reproducible**, with the residual recorded. If a 401 appears again, re-open with the timestamp and the profile that was running; do not re-arm this card on the old evidence.
